memory_update.text: AXTI should be treated as the primary US-listed underfollowed candidate for the precision-substrate node because its InP revenue is now majority data-center-linked and directly upstream of EML/silicon-photonics optical components.
VECO is a second-order bottleneck candidate for the same node: not a substrate supplier, but a tool supplier whose MOCVD, IBD, and wet-processing systems enable InP laser capacity expansion.
POET belongs in a speculative-shadow lane rather than the core substrate lane until production-volume orders, customer qualifications, and manufacturing yields are verified.

The hidden bottleneck may be more precisely framed as InP substrates plus InP laser/component manufacturing capacity for 800G/1.6T optical interconnects, rather than generic optical-transceiver substrates.

Need next-pass verification of customer identity, qualification-cycle length, export-permit risk, and whether AXTI/VECO revenue is tied to binding multi-quarter commitments versus pull-forward ordering.

node: Precision substrates and components for 800G/1.6T AI optical transceivers
summary: Layer 1B expansion finds that the most concrete underfollowed supply-chain exposure is indium phosphide substrate and InP laser/component manufacturing capacity, not only finished transceiver brands. AXTI is the cleanest small/mid-cap substrate candidate; VECO is a second-order equipment chokepoint for InP laser scaling; POET is a speculative optical-interposer/engine candidate tied to 800G/1.6T integration; LITE is included only as the reference anchor because its EML and laser products define downstream demand for InP substrates. No buy/sell recommendation is implied.
